transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Verdant Head of ML), Daniel (Verdant Platform), Aisha (Verdant SRE)

Summary:
Technical deep dive to triage recurring CUDA OOMs and watchdog timeouts in Verdant's private deployment. Focus areas: telemetry requirements, repro strategy, fallback/retry semantics, KV cache interactions, batching & quantization behavior, and on-prem considerations.

[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, I'll kick off. We're here to walk through the cuda oom and watchdog patterns you've been hitting, and agree the telemetry + repro steps.
[00:14] Priya: hey thanks, yeah we've been seeing intermittent OOMs on our on-prem boxes mostly p4d-like hosts behind our VPC. It's pretty disruptive.
[00:23] Daniel: pattern is mostly during large batch windows  heavy long-context requests and sometimes an existing session will hang until the watchdog kills the process.
[00:33] Liam: when you say hang, is it a kernel fault, a GPU reset, or a driver timeout?
[00:39] Aisha: logs show both: sometimes "CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED" and other times a watchdog timeout with GPU reset. The log snippet is in the doc we uploaded.
[00:52] Priya: there's also a flamegraph we captured with a cheap sampler but it's noisy.
[01:05] Maya: first pass questions: what's your model size, quant profile, and batching config?
[01:12] Daniel: model is 13B quantized to int8 per-channel via our converter; we keep fp16 checkpoint for fallbacks. We do dynamic batching with max_batch_tokens 8192 and session pinning.
[01:28] Liam: 8192 is significant  the runtime's KV cache memory and prefetching can spike. Do you have telemetry for peak allocation per stream? nvml shows abrupt jumps if prefetch is in-flight.
[01:42] Daniel: we have NVML snapshots but not per-stream detail.
[01:47] Aisha: platform prefetcher warms KV into GPU ahead of inference. We suspect a race where prefetch + large batch + quantized interpreter allocation cause fragmentation and soft OOMs.
[02:02] Priya: switching to fp16 reduces OOMs but increases latency.
[02:09] Maya: quant can reduce steady-state memory but increase transient spikes if dequant buffers are ephemeral and not pooled.
[02:20] Liam: two telemetry items that help: 1) per-allocation timestamps (size + stream id + backtrace if possible), 2) nsys traces on a reproducer until failure. Nsys will show kernel stall patterns like long memcpy on a stream followed by waiting launches.
[02:36] Daniel: nsys slows the system; should we run it on staging?
[02:41] Liam: yes, on staging with same driver. Capture dmesg around reset and /var/log/messages.
[02:49] Priya: what about KV eviction heuristics? We saw evictions before failures.
[02:55] Maya: eviction + prefetch can cause double allocations: evict prefix KV to free space then prefetch synchronously later causing spikes. Do evictions include sizes in logs?
[03:09] Aisha: evictions log session ids but not sizes.
[03:16] Liam: add sizes and UUIDs per alloc. Also sample process GPU memory every 50ms for a 10s window around the event.
[03:29] Priya: ok.
[03:31] Daniel: can Redwood runtime tolerate GPU reset and restart worker without losing in-flight requests?
[03:39] Maya: hosted mode fails requests and falls back to replicas. In private we can enable a restart supervisor to drain and rehydrate KV, but that increases tail latency and requires retries.
[03:55] Liam: runtime preserves idempotency only if clients supply idempotency tokens. Without them, retries risk duplicate side effects.
[04:07] Priya: our app does immediate retry on 5xx; not idempotent.
[04:12] Maya: add idempotency keys and use at-most-once semantics for critical flows.
[04:18] Aisha: exponential backoff vs immediate retry?
[04:21] Liam: immediate retry after reset often hits same failing resources. Use jitter + increasing backoff and route to a different pool/model variant (fp16 or smaller batch).
[04:35] Daniel: can runtime auto-degrade model or throttle batching on allocation pressure?
[04:41] Liam: yes: policies can reduce max_batch_tokens, disable prefetch, or route to fallback. Need reliable signals: sustained allocation failures, consecutive watchdog resets, or fragmentation metrics.
[04:59] Priya: fragmentation: free memory exists but cannot allocate contiguous block. Is that GPU-level fragmentation?
[05:06] Liam: yes. CUDA allocations can fail due to fragmentation or pool exhaustion. Fixes: pooling allocator, pre-reserve scratch buffers, bump pool size, reuse buffers, align allocator to kernel needs.
[05:20] Maya: run periodic full-GPU defrag hooks during low-traffic windows if runtime supports it.
[05:28] Aisha: can Redwood expose more granular metrics? We only get process-level mem and per-request token timing.
[05:35] Maya: enable enhanced telemetry for Private: per-allocation logs, KV occupancy by session, batching queue lengths. It adds overhead but is useful for triage.
[05:45] Daniel: enable it for staging.
[05:48] Priya: int8 kernels sometimes need extra scratch workspace; cuBLASLt workspace can push you over. Capture CUBLAS workspace queries.
[06:12] Aisha: how to get those?
[06:16] Liam: enable cublas logging env vars and record cudnn & cublas workspace queries in the nsys trace; algorithm ids appear there.
[06:26] Priya: ok.
[06:28] Maya: any NIC flaps or host issues correlated?
[06:34] Daniel: occasional NIC flaps; we'll include system logs.
[06:39] Liam: include ethtool, dmesg, kubelet logs. GPU errors can be downstream of host instability.
[06:48] Priya: good.
[06:50] Maya: define reproducible test: 1) 13B model quant int8 with fp16 fallback, 2) ramp synthetic traffic with 90th pct token lengths, 3) enable KV prefetch and toggle off in runs, 4) capture nsys and nvml, 5) measure tail-latency and OOMs.
[07:12] Daniel: actionable. We'll set up staging.
[07:16] Aisha: runtime backoff config?
[07:20] Liam: runtime exposes attempts, base_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, and route_policy (same-pool vs alternate-pool). For private set route_policy to alternate-pool to avoid hot nodes.
[07:33] Priya: route based on error class?
[07:38] Maya: yes: map error codes to actions. CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED -> alternate pool + reduce batch; WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT -> immediate route + longer backoff.
[07:52] Daniel: we want recommended defaults.
[07:57] Maya: we'll propose after reviewing traces.
[08:01] Liam: operational idea: short-lived probe alloc on GPU every N seconds; if probe fails, it's a canary for fragmentation.
[08:12] Priya: if canary fails proactively stop prefetch or reduce queue?
[08:17] Liam: exactly.
[08:19] Aisha: kernel retries vs process restart?
[08:26] Liam: kernel retries are risky; driver won't retry crashed kernel. Better to fail request quickly, restart worker, rehydrate state. For small transient alloc failures a retry with backoff may succeed.
[08:40] Maya: recommend policy: 1 soft-retry with small backoff for alloc failures (non-watchdog), 2nd failure -> drain worker, restart, route.
[08:52] Priya: sounds good.
[08:54] Daniel: logging formats?
[08:58] Liam: standardize fields: timestamp, pid, process-id, gpu-id, error-class, cuda-error-code, allocator-request-size, free-memory, kv-occupied-bytes, batch-id, session-id. Log as JSON lines.
[09:12] Aisha: we'll add those.
[09:14] Priya: perf regressions after quantization?
[09:19] Liam: int8 speedups depend on kernel support and workspace choices; algorithm selection affects speed. Lock algorithms after profiling across shapes.
[09:33] Daniel: ok.
[09:36] Maya: Redwood will create a "GPU health" dashboard: OOM count, watchdog resets, fragmentation probe fail rate, avg free contiguous block size, KV occupancy, batching queue depth, per-request tail latency.
[09:52] Priya: yes please.
[09:55] Maya: enhanced telemetry streams metadata; ensure KMS is configured and logs go to secure storage behind your VPC.
[10:07] Daniel: we use internal S3 with KMS; will provide access.
[10:12] Aisha: HSM/KMS considerations for KV rehydration?
[10:17] Maya: runtime needs decrypt permissions on boot; for air-gapped mount secrets via secure vault. We'll include in checklist.
[10:27] Priya: great.
[10:29] Maya: any other edges?
[10:31] Daniel: we saw a one-off device-side assert that killed the process; is that a kernel bug?
[10:40] Liam: device-side assert often from out-of-bounds indices or dtype mismatches in custom kernels; capture kernel stack and input tensor shapes.
[10:50] Priya: ok.
[10:51] Maya: recap telemetry needs: nsys + nvml traces, per-allocation logs, eviction events with sizes, cublas workspace queries, dmesg, kubelet logs, sample workloads.
[11:07] Aisha: noted.
[11:09] Daniel: will share model and 24h sample by Monday.
[11:13] Maya: Redwood will provide repro harness, recommended runtime policy, enhanced telemetry config, and dashboard.
[11:21] Priya: thank you. Immediate mitigation?
[11:26] Liam: short-term: reduce max_batch_tokens to 4096, disable prefetch, enable alternate-pool routing.
[11:36] Daniel: we'll apply on staging now.
[11:38] Maya: perfect.
[11:40] Liam: also set retries to 2 with base_backoff 200ms and max_backoff 2s for non-idempotent flows.
[11:49] Aisha: ok.
[11:51] Maya: blockers?
[11:53] Priya: none.
[11:55] Daniel: we'll upload artifacts.
[11:58] Maya: action items recap: Liam to run traces and share; Daniel to upload model and samples; Maya to send docs and quote. Follow-up canary next week.
[12:12] Priya: thanks everyone.
[12:16] Maya: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
